ai.title: Docs update model descriptions for lite and max modes
ai.summary: Documentation files updated to reflect current model routing for --lite and --max modes. --lite now describes Gemini 2.5 Flash Thinking (~1/5 cost), while --max describes a hybrid of Gemini 2.5 Pro and Claude Sonnet. FAQ and keyboard shortcut docs also updated to include Gemini 2.5 Pro for thinking in --max mode.

eli5.text: The written guides that explain how the assistant works have been updated to match the actual models now used for two of its operating modes. When you select the budget-friendly mode, the documentation now correctly reflects that a faster, lower-cost model is being used, and the high-quality mode description has been adjusted to describe the mix of models that handle more complex tasks. If you read these guide pages today, you will see wording about the current model setup instead of outdated references to previous models, so the printed explanation now lines up with what the assistant actually does behind the scenes.

ai.title: Add gpt4.1 to experimental mode
ai.summary: gpt4.1 now serves the 'agent' operation when costMode is 'experimental'. This expands the experimental tier beyond gemini2_5_flash_thinking, which remains the default for 'lite'. The change occurs in common/src/constants.ts within getModelForMode. Experimental mode now routes to models.gpt4_1.

eli5.text: People who opt into the experimental mode of the assistant can now choose a different AI model named gpt4.1 for handling tasks. This only applies to the experimental mode, which already let users pick another model called gemini2_5_flash_thinking; the default mode for most users stays the same. As of today, enabling experimental mode routes your requests to this newer model, which may handle reasoning tasks differently. If you do not use experimental mode, nothing about your experience changes.

ai.title: Tighten thinking stream prompt brevity
ai.summary: Updated system guidelines in `backend/src/thinking-stream.ts` to enforce shorter thinking sessions. Changed permissive wording to 'highly recommended' and added explicit 'Keep your thinking as short as possible!' instruction. Affects internal reasoning token generation logic.

eli5.text: When you ask a question that requires some thought, the assistant's internal reasoning process has been quietly trimmed to be shorter and more to the point. Instead of letting it ramble through lengthy internal monologues, the updated guidance now strongly encourages it to keep its deliberations brief especially when the next step is already clear. If you were watching from behind the scenes you would notice the assistant finishing its thinking phase sooner and jumping straight to an answer, rather than lingering in a long internal dialogue.

ai.title: Add /init command and JSONC config support
ai.summary: Introduced `/init` command triggering a specific system prompt to initialize or update project configuration files. Config parser now supports `codebuff.jsonc` with comments via `jsonc-parser`, prioritizing it over `codebuff.json`. System instructions are wrapped in `<system_instructions>` tags for better model adherence. The `description` field was added to `CodebuffConfigSchema` as an optional, non-functional marker.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant inside a project, you can now type a setup command that walks you through creating your configuration file instead of having to write it by hand or know its exact format. The configuration file can now be written with helpful comments included, the same way you'd annotate a document, and the assistant will read and follow those extra notes. Behind the scenes, the instructions the assistant receives are wrapped in a clearly marked section so it treats them as firm guidance rather than casual notes, and a short optional description field can be added to that configuration file to label what it's for without affecting how things work.

ai.title: Add /config webpage and schema display component
ai.summary: New `/config` page redirects to docs anchor. `SchemaDisplay` component renders `CodebuffConfigSchema` via `stringifySchema`. `stringify-schema.ts` refactored for better LLM/human readability (indentation, object handling). `constants.ts` descriptions trimmed. Docs content `config.mdx` added.

eli5.text: You can now visit /config on the Codebuff website, which takes you straight to the configuration documentation section. The page that displays the structure of the configuration file has been redesigned so both the assistant and people reading the docs can follow its layout more easily, with clearer descriptions and nesting. When you run the setup command that creates a starter configuration file on your computer, it now points to this same /config address. If you open your browser and go to /config today, you will land on the documentation page that explains every option you can set in your configuration file.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to create a brand-new file, it now writes out the complete file from start to finish instead of leaving placeholder comments where content is missing. Previously, the assistant could accidentally produce incomplete stubs for new files by skipping sections it hadn't written yet. This change makes new file creation more reliable by ensuring the entire file is filled in, while still allowing the assistant to use shortcuts when modifying existing files.

Any developer on the team who opens their coding tools will now see automatic error reports appear in a shared log file, whereas before the checker was disabled and not actively watching for problems. These statuses travel alongside the existing set of behind-the-scenes flags the assistant uses to coordinate setup screens, so when you start a new project the assistant will know whether it already collected your API key and preferences or needs to prompt you again. The code that names and reads those flags was reorganized to make room for the new ones, and the way they are imported and tracked was tightened up at the same time, but from your perspective the main difference is that configuration prompts should appear at the right moment instead of being skipped or repeated. The two new statuses

eli5.text: The assistant's training data is now cleaner: when pulling past examples to learn from, the system grabs only the newest annotation per example instead of duplicates, so it won't get confused by seeing the same case twice. You probably wouldn't notice this directly, but it means the next model that gets taught from this data learns from a tidier, less repetitive set of examples. The data collection also pulls in up to ten times more examples per batch and skips any single example that's absurdly long, keeping the training files focused and readable. This is internal cleanup to how the teaching material gets assembled, not something that changes how the assistant behaves today.

ai.title: Windows process group killing
ai.summary: Added `killProcessTreeSoftly` to handle Windows process termination. Uses `taskkill /T` on `win32` and `process.kill(-pid, 'SIGTERM')` on POSIX. Replaces direct `process.kill` calls in `killAndWait`, `sendKillSignalToAllBackgroundProcesses`, and `cleanupStoredProcesses` within `npm-app/src/background-process-manager.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant needs to shut down background tasks on a Windows computer, it now tells the whole family of related processes to stop together, instead of just one. This prevents leftover helper processes from sticking around after a session ends. You wouldn't notice this unless you were watching the task list on Windows, where previously some hidden processes might have stayed running after you closed the app.
